_comment: Scenarios for src/api/login.js: login() is run against a fake panel and must resolve to expected.zoneTuples or reject with expected.error (exact message). Unless a row says otherwise the panel behaves like mock_paradox.js with session value 91AC25D06A0C26BA, accepts the u/p of crypto.json 'sample session, 4 digit code' (username user, password 1234) and lists the six sample zones. 'panel' overrides the answer for one request path: a response or a list of responses used in order; each response is {file} (relative to tests/), {body}, {status[, headers][, body]} (200, no extra headers and an empty body when omitted), {zones} (the index page with these [enabled, name] slots, padded to 32 slots with [0, ' '] like the real panel), {zones_by_slot} (the same, sparse: slot index -> [enabled, name]), {destroy} (the connection is reset) or {hang} (never answered); 'times' limits how often a response is used (forever when omitted). 'expected.default_query' is the exact query string of the first /default.html request. 'expected.request_counts' is how often the panel was asked for each path (a path that is not listed was never asked; one request to each of /logout.html, /login_page.html, /default.html and /index.html when the whole object is omitted). 'expected.warnings' are the messages logged with console.warn (none when omitted). Error messages starting with 'Request failed' come from axios and 'socket hang up' / 'connect ECONNREFUSED' from Node's http client: a port only has to fail there. Rows that pin a defect on purpose (known_bug) are in known_bugs/login_cases.json, in the same groups.

login.name: captured login, default and index pages of a real panel give the six enabled zones
disabled slots are dropped and enabled names are kept exactly as given
flag values other than 1 are dropped
no enabled zone gives an empty list
an empty tbl_zone array gives an empty list
a list of one zone is read completely
zone names of letters, digits, underscore and spaces are accepted
an index page without tbl_zone makes login fail
the login page in place of the index page makes login fail without a retry
login.note: Retries cover failed requests only; a 200 page that does not parse ends login at once (one /index.html request).
